summary: Buffered file read driver. When the stream object is valid and its type byte at a1+92 equals 119, resets the buffer at a1+4 and repeatedly tops up a 0x4000-byte buffer, reads 1 byte through FileReadWrapperWithLock, then hands each chunk to sub_535E80 to parse it. Returns 1 (mapped to 0) when parsing reports more data pending, the parser status otherwise, -1 on a short read, or -2 when the stream type guard fails.

operations.description: Proceed only when the stream pointer is non-null and the type byte at a1+92 equals 119 (0x77, 'w'); otherwise return -2.
Reset the buffered byte counter at a1+4 to 0 before the read loop.
While the buffer is not yet full (a1+16 != 0x4000), compute the remaining space as 0x4000 minus the current buffered byte count and attempt to fill it.
Call FileReadWrapperWithLock with the file handle at a1+72, size 1, the remaining space, and the target buffer at a1+64; treat a short read as a fatal error.
On a short read, set the status at a1+56 to -1 and return -1.
On a successful fill, mark the buffer full by setting a1+16 to 0x4000 and record the file handle from a1+72 at a1+12.
Call sub_535E80 with the stream and parse context; store its returned parse status at a1+56.
When the buffer is exactly full and parsing returns -5, coerce the stored status at a1+56 to 0.
Continue parsing while either the buffer still holds unread bytes (a1+16 non-zero) or parsing reports status 1 (more data available); stop when the stored status is 2 or higher.
Return 0 when the final status is 1, otherwise return the final stored status at a1+56.

unresolved: Layout and meaning of the stream object (offsets a1+4/12/16/56/64/72/92 referenced only in source) are not formally classified in the packet fields list.
Meaning of the parse status constants (-5, 1, 2+) from sub_535E80 is not derivable from this function alone.
